articles.headline: Cooper Kupp returns Tom Brady's whiteboard with a bracket: Shake and Bake (12) cannot be allowed to beat Gods Favorite Jew (11)
articles.dek: Shake and Bake are 1-13 with the league's fewest points, 757.12, and are projected 138.13 to 132.09 over 2-12 Gods Favorite Jew. Kupp and AJ Barner say that margin is the problem.
body: Cooper Kupp brought the whiteboard back on Wednesday morning. It had been missing from Shake and Bake's meeting room since the Seattle caucus took it two weeks ago, and head coach Tom Brady received it at the door with what witnesses described as visible relief. The relief lasted until he turned it over.

On the back, in Kupp's handwriting, was a bracket. It listed every remaining Shake and Bake opponent, a projected margin for each, and a column headed 'Acceptable?' Against Gods Favorite Jew, Thursday-to-Monday's opponent, Kupp had written 'NO' and underlined it twice. Shake and Bake are 1-13, have scored 757.12 points, and are projected 138.13 to Gods Favorite Jew's 132.09. Kupp's position is that a six-point projected edge is not something a team in their situation should be proud of.

'We are one win from becoming a different franchise,' Kupp said in the corridor, declining to say which franchise. 'I did not come here to be competitive. I came here to be consistent.' AJ Barner, standing beside him with a clipboard he was not asked to bring, said the caucus had already voted 2-0 to oppose a win and that the result was binding. Nobody had authorised the vote. Barner entered it in the minutes anyway, and the minutes are also on the whiteboard.

Brady called the bracket 'a document' and asked for it to be removed from his wall. Kupp replied that the wall was never his, since the whiteboard had been in Seattle's custody for fourteen days and the caucus had paid for the marker. Brady then spent twenty minutes establishing that a head coach may not be told by his own wide receiver which games to lose, and that he in fact has no written rule saying so. He is now drafting one. It runs to two pages.

Cam Ward, who is the team's quarterback and has been left out of every document so far, was seen reading the bracket for a long time. He asked only whether the column applied to him. Kupp told him it applied to everyone and asked him to sign at the bottom.

Across the league, Gods Favorite Jew, 2-12 with 865.74 points, have not been consulted and have not been told they are the opponent of a protest. Geno Smith is their quarterback and has nothing to say. Shake and Bake's own record is the only thing both sides agree on. The whiteboard is back on the wall, facing the wall.

articles.headline: The Ripple Effect 👑 (3) beat The Phantom Troupe (2) 205.5-172.82 for Week 7's top score

Only Muffin Toppers, at 172.94, scored more than Phantom Troupe among the teams that did not play them. It still was not close.

The Tax had Caleb Williams at 27.52 but got 9.7 from Kenneth Walker III, 9.4 from Justin Jefferson and 4.1 from Aaron Jones Sr.
Commercial Break (7) beat Chinese Sweatshop (8) by 39.5, 153.12 to 113.62. KC Concepcion Jr. supplied 26.2 against a projection of 12.02.

articles.headline: THE REFUGEES (6) land Tanner McKee from THE TAX (5) for a 2028 third, then play them this week
articles.dek: Both teams are 8-6. REFUGEES add the quarterback and send their own 2028 third-round pick to The Tax, their Week 8 opponent.
body: THE REFUGEES (6) and THE TAX (5) completed a two-asset trade: REFUGEES receive quarterback Tanner McKee, and The Tax receive REFUGEES' own 2028 third-round pick. Nothing else changed hands.

The teams are level at 8-6. REFUGEES have scored 1138.8 points and allowed 1086.4. The Tax have scored 1192 and allowed 1153.88. Week 8 puts them head to head, with The Tax projected at 210.01 and REFUGEES at 174.61.

McKee does not appear in either side's Week 8 lineup, so the trade does nothing to those projections. REFUGEES' quarterback is Josh Allen, projected 37.35, the highest figure at the position on the board. The Tax have Caleb Williams at 24.95 and Michael Penix Jr. at 23.89, and neither is affected by the deal.

That makes this a roster-building move rather than a Week 8 one. REFUGEES paid for a quarterback with a third-round pick, and The Tax took the pick and parted with a player who was not in their starting group. The pick is REFUGEES' own, so its value will follow how REFUGEES finish, not anything The Tax do.
Last week REFUGEES lost to Dead Sons 191.4 to 139.5, with Shedeur Sanders in the lineup and scoring nothing. The Tax lost by 3.26 to Beasty Boys.

REFUGEES answer with RJ Harvey, Jaylen Waddle and Zonovan Knight in the same Broncos-Cardinals game, and Detroit's LaPorta (19.35) and Williams (17.24) against the Packers. Elsewhere, Gods Favorite Jew lead Muffin Toppers 82.44 to 63.4. Muffin Toppers have Jordan Love and Matthew Golden against Detroit, while Gods Favorite Jew's Blake Corum, Courtland Sutton and Kendrick Bourne are all still ahead of them. Chinese Sweatshop trail Commercial Break 100.38 to 42.22 and need Ashton Jeanty, Michael Mayer and Matthew Stafford in Raiders-Rams to do most of the repair work.

articles.headline: Colston Loveland invoices Parkers Dead Sons (9) for 'Thursday', Richard Sherman rejects the paperwork
articles.dek: Dead Sons are 3-9 but lead THE REFUGEES (6) 36.3-0 after Loveland's 24.4. Loveland has since submitted a bill for the lead, a scouting report on Jaxon Smith-Njigba and a request for a nameplate.
body: Colston Loveland arrived at Parkers Dead Sons headquarters on Friday morning with a binder, a label maker and an invoice. The invoice, addressed to head coach Richard Sherman, billed the team for 'services rendered, Thursday, one (1) lead', itemised at 24.4 points, the most any tight end in the league scored in Week 7's opening game.

Sherman returned the invoice unopened. 'He's been paid,' the coach said. 'He's on the roster. That is the payment.' Loveland replied that the roster was a courtesy and the 36.3-0 lead over THE REFUGEES was a product, and asked whether Dead Sons wished to continue receiving it.

The numbers back the lead and very little else. Dead Sons are 3-9, have scored 855.3 points and have allowed 949.48, and sit ninth in the poll. Loveland was projected for 13.96 on Thursday and nearly doubled it. Rome Odunze added 11.9 beside him, and a Dead Sons staffer confirmed that Odunze 'was not consulted about the invoice and would like it noted that he was also there.'

By midday Loveland had moved on to a ten-page scouting report on Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Dead Sons' other headline name, who plays Sunday night and carries a projection of 31.3, the highest of any receiver on the slate. The report grades Smith-Njigba 'adequate, pending Loveland's endorsement' and recommends he 'stop standing in the good light'. Smith-Njigba, who had not been asked, declined to comment and was seen moving his locker nameplate two stalls down the hall. It was on the wall again by lunch, with Loveland's label maker next to it.

Sherman held a short meeting in the film room to settle it. Loveland attended and asked for the room to be renamed, then asked to be excused from the room. He was not excused. Sherman locked the door from outside and kept the binder.

None of this is final. REFUGEES, 8-4, are projected for 165.59 to Dead Sons' 211.47, and they have a full Sunday of Detroit, Cincinnati, Denver and San Francisco players to close a 36.3-point gap. Dead Sons have Smith-Njigba, Bo Nix and Jared Goff still to play. Loveland says he will be watching from the facility's best chair, which he has labelled.

The Phantom Troupe (11-1) took 64 points and the other three firsts. Last week Lip-Pickers held all seven first-place votes and a perfect 84, so the field closed fast. Phantom Troupe move up from third to second, past The Ripple Effect. Ripple Effect are 8-4 and have scored 1,127.38 points, the most in the league, but no voter put them first. They took 61 points, no lower than fourth on any ballot, and fall one place. Muffin Toppers hold fourth at 11-1 with 54 points, level with Phantom Troupe on record and two places behind on the ballots.

The middle of the table has the week's biggest move. Chinese Sweatshop climb two places to eighth with 29 points. They are 4-8, and the ballots put them ahead of Parkers Dead Sons (3-9, 26 points), who slip to ninth. articles.headline: Cooper Kupp and AJ Barner convene Seattle caucus, seize Tom Brady's whiteboard at Shake and Bake (12), 1-11 and 97.9 points behind Lip-Pickers (2)
articles.dek: Shake and Bake have the fewest points in the league, 664.28, and are projected 122.54 to 220.44 against Latina Lip-Pickers. Two Seattle starters say the team's problem is Tuesday's schedule, and have taken the whiteboard to prove it.
body: Cooper Kupp and AJ Barner called a meeting of the Seattle caucus on Tuesday morning, and by the time it ended Shake and Bake head coach Tom Brady no longer had a whiteboard. Both men describe this as a seizure. Brady describes it as a theft. The whiteboard is, at the time of writing, in Kupp's car.

The caucus is two members and a chair. Kupp chairs. Barner was, by his own account, informed he was a member in the parking lot. Their agenda has one item: Shake and Bake are 1-11, have scored 664.28 points, the fewest in the league, and have not once, in Kupp's reading, been asked what Seattle thinks.

"Everything on this roster that works wears a Seattle jersey," Kupp told the room, which was also the car. Kupp is projected for 8.75 on Sunday night. Barner is projected for 10.63. Kupp's position is that projections are a bureaucratic instrument and that the caucus does not recognise them.

He has history with paperwork. Last week he filed a motion asking the league to declare Week 6 over after Shake and Bake led THE TAX 15.1 to 0 on Thursday night. The league did not rule on the motion. THE TAX scored 186.6, the week's top score, and Shake and Bake finished on 88.88. Kupp has since re-filed the motion with the new total attached and a request that the earlier ruling be considered void for want of a ruling.

Brady, who is the team's head coach and has seven championship rings of his own, responded with a laminated memo reassigning every locker in the building. Kupp has been moved beside the ice machine. Barner has been moved nearer the ice machine. Cam Ward, projected for 21.63 and the only Shake and Bake starter with a quarterback's confidence, has been given the corner locker and told nothing, which the caucus has read as a bribe.

The caucus has issued three demands. First, a Tuesday schedule that begins after lunch. Second, formal recognition of Seattle as a voting bloc. Third, the return of Kupp's original locker, which he says had a better view of the door. Brady has agreed to none of them and has asked for the whiteboard back, in writing, with a pen he does not have.

The stakes on the field are less ornate. Lip-Pickers are 10-2, scored 1,108.78 points this season and are projected 97.9 ahead of Shake and Bake. Sunday night's Seattle-Kansas City game is the only thing either member of the caucus can control, and Kupp has said he will be wearing the whiteboard's marker in his sock.

Asked whether the seizure would help Shake and Bake's record, Kupp said the record was never the point, and that the point would be announced after the next meeting. The next meeting is scheduled for the car.

Moving Coleman for a pick fits a team that is looking beyond the next few weeks, and the second-rounder is the kind of asset that buys a bigger move later.
Commercial Break have not said what they plan to do with the pick. The Phantom Troupe have not said where Coleman fits. Both teams get what they asked for.

articles.headline: Three tight ends lock themselves in a meeting room over who leads Gods Favorite Jew (11), 1-9 and facing Beasty Boys💩 (9)
articles.dek: Mark Andrews, Hunter Henry and Kyle Pitts have filed competing seniority claims. The team has scored 601.5 points, the second-fewest in the league, and enters Week 6 as an 18.15-point underdog.
body: Mark Andrews, Hunter Henry and Kyle Pitts have been in the same windowless meeting room since Tuesday morning, and none of them will say who has the key. Gods Favorite Jew (11) are 1-9 and have scored 601.5 points, better only than Shake and Bake. All three tight ends are projected to start Sunday, which is the problem.

Andrews arrived first and put a laminated sheet on the door reading "Senior Tight End, Office Hours 9 to 11." Henry crossed out "Senior" and wrote "Acting." Pitts then taped up a document of his own titled Statement of Draft Position, which he says settles the matter and which he declines to attach. Nobody in the room has been able to say who is supposed to review it.

"I am not here to be difficult," Andrews said through the door. "I am here to be recognised. Three of us, one ranking, and I am TE14. That is the highest of the three and it has been entered into the minutes." The minutes are being kept by Henry, who is TE15 and has recorded that Andrews is not the chair.

Pitts, projected 11.72 and TE19, rejects the premise of the ranking. He has called the other two a committee, and says he will take no instruction from a committee. Late Tuesday he requested a separate table. The request was granted, and the table was placed beside the first one.

The stakes are real. Gods Favorite Jew's projection of 155.57 trails Beasty Boys💩 (9) at 173.72, and Beasty Boys are 2-8 themselves, so this is not a game anyone can afford to open with a sit-in. Beasty Boys head coach Nick Chubb has so far taken no position on the dispute, though a source close to the facility confirms he has asked for his chair back.

Kendrick Bourne, who is not a tight end and was not invited, has been seen at the door twice holding a coffee. He has been told the room is full. Brock Purdy, who does not play until Monday night, has been informed of nothing and is believed to be content with that.

All three Gods Favorite Jew tight ends play on Sunday afternoon. Pitts and Atlanta host Chicago, Andrews and Baltimore visit Cleveland, and Henry and New England host the Jets. They will have to leave the room for that, and a joint statement says they will go as separate parties, in separate cars, with the seniority question left open.

articles.headline: Cooper Kupp files scouting report on Darnell Mooney as Shake and Bake (12) face Chinese Sweatshop (10) as 38.75-point underdogs
articles.dek: Head coach Tom Brady has scheduled a vote on the findings. Shake and Bake are 1-7 with 492.1 points for, the second-fewest in the league.
body: Cooper Kupp submitted a nine-page scouting report on a teammate Friday morning, and the teammate is Darnell Mooney. The report is stapled, tabbed and addressed to head coach Tom Brady. Its central finding is that Mooney is projected for 6.34 points against Washington on Sunday, the lowest figure of any starter in the league this week.

Kupp himself is projected for 8.41. He was unmoved by the distinction. "Eight point four one is a number a man can build on," he told the film room, which by then had been cleared of everyone but Mooney, who had not been told the meeting was about him and had brought a sandwich.

The report's second section deals with Sunday's opponent. Shake and Bake are 1-7, and Chinese Sweatshop are also 1-7, but the two sides are not equals on paper: Sweatshop are projected for 176.47 and Shake and Bake for 137.72, a gap of 38.75. Kupp wants it noted that he did not draw up the projections and that he has asked for them to be redone. Nobody has told him who does that.

Brady, in his capacity as head coach, has declined to rule on the report and has called a vote instead. Ballots are to be handwritten. Quinshon Judkins asked whether the vote was binding and was told that it would be if it came out the right way. A seating chart for the vote has been laminated. Mooney's seat is at the far end, next to the projector, which Brady says is a coincidence.

Kupp's case is not all complaint. He points out that Cam Ward is projected at 21.23 and that Bhayshul Tuten, at 19.01, is the highest-projected player on the roster. He argues the team is one good Sunday from a respectable total, which is a position Shake and Bake have yet to reach in eight tries. They have scored 492.1 over the season, and only Gods Favorite Jew, at 483.36, has scored less.

Mooney's reply, relayed through a second sandwich, was that the projection was written by people who have never seen him move. He has asked that the report be read aloud, in full, before the vote. Brady has agreed, on the condition that Mooney reads it.

The matchup is the whole case, and both sides are at zero. Mooney plays at 1 p.m. Eastern in Washington. Kupp's Seattle game follows in the late window against San Francisco. If the report is right, the vote is academic. If it is wrong, Kupp has put a nine-page document on the record about a man who is sitting next to the projector.

articles.headline: DK Metcalf opens a rival practice in the car park of Chinese Sweatshop (10), 1-7 and attending neither
articles.dek: Player development coach Tyler Lockett has reassigned three lockers and issued a memo. The team has the week's most plausible reason for all of it: 572.28 points for, one win.
body: DK Metcalf has been running his own practice since Tuesday afternoon, in the car park behind the Chinese Sweatshop (10) facility, and by every account it is better attended than the official one.

Metcalf marked out a field with cones taken from the equipment room and put a folding table at midfield. On the table is a sign-in sheet. By Wednesday morning it carried four names, none of them his, and a fifth in what staff described as an unfamiliar hand. The team is 1-7 with 572.28 points for and 649.08 against. Metcalf says that record is the reason for the practice. Nobody has located the practice he says it is replacing.

Tyler Lockett, the team's player development coach, answered with a memo. It runs to two pages and is titled Concerning the Development of Persons Outside the Development Programme. It states that Metcalf's session is not recognised, that the cones are the property of the club, and that any player found developing without supervision will be reassigned to the locker beside the boiler. Lockett then reassigned three lockers. Metcalf's went to Tre' Harris. Harris did not ask for it and has been seen carrying his own shoes in a bag since.

Metcalf says Lockett has misread the situation. He told reporters his practice runs on what the team has produced, and the team has produced one win in eight tries. He described the 'real' programme as a ceremony with a whistle. He was then asked whether the cones would be returned. He said the cones were on loan, which is a matter of record, because Lockett's memo says so.

The standoff arrives in a week when Chinese Sweatshop are the favourites, which has done nothing for the mood. They are projected for 179.35 against Shake and Bake's 138.9, another 1-7 side with the league's second-lowest scoring. Matthew Stafford is projected for 28.19 in Monday night's Rams game, and the Sunday group of Ashton Jeanty, Metcalf himself and Tre' Harris carries most of the rest. Metcalf was asked if he would turn up for those. He said he would be there, on his own schedule, from a different car park.
Lockett has called a staff meeting for Thursday. Metcalf has called one for the same hour in the same room and says the first booking was his. Both have asked the other to bring chairs.

articles.headline: Latina Lip-Pickers (2) take Drake London from Beasty Boys💩 (9) as three trades reshape Week 5
articles.dek: Ethan was on both Tuesday deals for the 7-1 Lip-Pickers, Phantom Troupe (4) picked up Ollie Gordon, and Dead Sons (7) paid two 2028 picks for Jared Goff.
body: Three trades completed on Tuesday, and Lip-Pickers were in two of them. The biggest came late: Latina Lip-Pickers (7-1) acquired Drake London from Beasty Boys (2-6) and sent back De'Von Achane, their 2027 first-round pick, their 2028 third and a 2027 second that originally belonged to Muffin Toppers. Beasty Boys also sent Lip-Pickers their own 2027 third plus their 2028 second and fourth.

London is projected for 23.7 in Atlanta's Sunday night game against Baltimore, the fifth-highest receiver projection this week. He joins a Lip-Pickers lineup that already carries CeeDee Lamb and Ja'Marr Chase, and that faces THE REFUGEES. Lip-Pickers have scored 759.92 points, second in the league, so this is a team adding to a strength. Beasty Boys have scored 598.04 and are projected well behind Muffin Toppers in their own matchup. They get a running back and several picks that were Lip-Pickers' to give.

The Muffin Toppers second-rounder that Lip-Pickers passed along had arrived hours earlier. In the first Tuesday deal, Lip-Pickers sent Ollie Gordon and a 2027 third-round pick that began with Chinese Sweatshop to The Phantom Troupe, and took that Muffin Toppers second in return. Gordon is projected for 19.64 against Cincinnati on Sunday, and Phantom Troupe (7-1) are already working through questionable and missing receivers. They gave up the second-round pick to get him.

Dead Sons (3-5) made the other move. They sent a 2028 second-round pick that began with Muffin Toppers and a 2028 third that began with Chinese Sweatshop to Shake and Bake (1-7) and received Jared Goff. Goff is projected for 32.67 at Arizona, the second-best quarterback number on the board, and he lands on a roster that already has Bo Nix and Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Dead Sons have scored 582.22 and allowed 578.64, so their record is worse than their points. Their 221.24 projection is one of the two highest in Week 5.

Shake and Bake have scored 492.1 points, among the lowest totals in the league. They collected two more picks and no player. Whether that helps next Sunday is a different matter, and the picks will not appear in this week's score.

articles.headline: THE TAX (6) beat Commercial Break (9) 196.34-144.4 as Tetairoa McMillan's 44.2 turns a Sunday afternoon deficit into a rout

body: THE TAX (6) had the best week in the league by the only measure that counts for a recap: they were losing and then they were not. Walker scored 34.4, the second-best running back total of the week, against a projection of 29.19. THE REFUGEES (4) won by the widest margin, 180.82 to 118.78 over Gods Favorite Jew (11). Tee Higgins scored 29.2 and Sam LaPorta 28.4, while Josh Allen delivered 21.72 on a projection of 35.53. Gods Favorite Jew are 1-7 with 483.36 points for, the lowest total in the league.

Chinese Sweatshop missed the median by 1.02 and sit at 1-7.

Parkers Dead Sons (7) beat Beasty Boys (8) 141.88-123.66, with Nico Collins scoring 30.3. Dead Sons are 3-5 and Beasty Boys 2-6. Dead Sons finished 3.26 short of the median, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba scored 13.1 against a projection of 29.39.

articles.headline: DeVonta Smith ruled out for The Phantom Troupe (5), the third starter listed Out ahead of a 1-7 opponent
articles.dek: Smith was projected for 15.93 in Philadelphia's trip to Jacksonville on Sunday morning. The 7-1 Phantom Troupe already have Ladd McConkey and Saquon Barkley listed out.
body: DeVonta Smith has been ruled out for Philadelphia's game at Jacksonville, and The Phantom Troupe had him in their Week 5 starting group. He was projected for 15.93 points, the 25th-ranked receiver on the week's projections, and the Eagles play at 9:30 a.m. Eastern on Sunday, which makes his the first game of the day for the team's starters.

It is the third Out designation among Phantom Troupe starters this week. McConkey and Barkley were covered after Sunday, when the team still posted 178.78 to beat Chinese Sweatshop by 34.66. Smith's status is new. The team is 7-1 with 690.1 points for and 569.74 against, and it opens Week 5 against Gods Favorite Jew, who are 1-7 and have scored 483.36 all season.

The matchup math does not suggest panic. Phantom Troupe's projection for the week is 198.29 against 153.04 for Gods Favorite Jew, and the projected points are concentrated elsewhere: Jahmyr Gibbs is projected for 36.04, the best number of any back this week, Drake Maye for 30.9 and Joe Burrow for 30.39. Zay Flowers, at 23.4, is the highest-projected receiver on the roster that is not on the injury list.

What Smith's absence changes is how many plausible options Phantom Troupe have left to cover for him. Chris Godwin is projected for 12.23, Jake Ferguson for 12.14 and Brenton Strange for 13.63, and none of those matches what Smith was expected to give them. That is a gap measured in a few points, not the kind that moves a 45-point projected margin, but it is the third of its kind and the team has not yet needed all of them to count.

Gods Favorite Jew would need an unusually large week from Brock Purdy and the rest of a group projected for 153.04. Their Monday game is behind them, and everything else on their side plays on Sunday. The Eagles' Smith, meanwhile, is not the only Philadelphia player on a rival roster in this league: THE TAX have Jalen Hurts and Dontayvion Wicks, who are not listed out.

articles.headline: Lamar Jackson and Patrick Mahomes both demand the QB slot on The Ripple Effect 👑 (1), neither will be the Super
articles.dek: The 4-2 team starts two quarterbacks in a league built for it. The quarterbacks would like it noted that only one of them is a flex.
body: Lamar Jackson and Patrick Mahomes have been sharing a lineup for the entire season without a word on the subject. Ben's Week 4 submission for The Ripple Effect 👑 (1) has now ended that peace. Both quarterbacks start, and the lineup form has a line that says QB and another that says SUPER_FLEX. Neither man will accept the second one.

"Super is a promotion," Jackson told reporters gathered around a lineup page that he insists is a locker room. "But it is written second, after FLEX, and I have never seen a starter at the bottom of the card describe himself as the headliner. I am the QB. I am projected for 35.89, which is the second-highest quarterback number this week. I am not discussing the order further."

Mahomes, projected at 32.5, countered that the Super slot is wasted on a man who is not the best quarterback on the card, and that he has played the position long enough to know what a flex is. "A flex is Kalif Raymond," he said. Raymond is projected for 12.32 points, the lowest of the ten starters, and is listed as WR42 for the week. Raymond declined to comment, but is starting.

Mahomes then turned to his own supporting cast. Travis Kelce and Rashee Rice both start for Muffin Toppers. Kenneth Walker starts for THE TAX. Tyquan Thornton starts for Shake and Bake. All four wear the same helmet as Mahomes, and none of them are on the roster he throws for. "I am in a lineup with strangers," he said. Jackson's own situation is similar: Derrick Henry is with Muffin Toppers, Zay Flowers is with Phantom Troupe, and Mark Andrews and Rashod Bateman are with Gods Favorite Jew. "Please do not bring that up," Jackson said.

The timing is awkward for a team with a lot going for it. The Ripple Effect are 4-2, have scored 593.68 points, the second-most in the league, and carry the biggest projection on the board at 251.83 against 157.01 for Shake and Bake. Right now they also trail that opponent 24.6 to 0, all of it Quinshon Judkins on Thursday night, with the entire roster still to play. Jackson plays first, at 1 p.m. against Tennessee. Mahomes follows at 4:25 at Las Vegas.

"That gives me three and a half hours to be the QB before he is," Jackson said. Mahomes said the slot is assigned by the form and the form has no opinion on kickoff times. Asked who would settle it, both men said the points, and then both said they would settle it first.

articles.headline: Quinshon Judkins, 24.6 points into Friday, asks Shake and Bake (12) to stop calling him a piece of the offense
articles.dek: The Cleveland back is the only Shake and Bake starter to have played this week and says the 1-5 team's 351.94 points for are now a separate accounting matter.
body: Quinshon Judkins arrived at Shake and Bake (12) headquarters on Friday morning with a one-page document titled "Terms of Continued Participation." He was projected for 16.18 points on Thursday night. He scored 24.6, the best running back line of the week so far, and has since asked that all internal correspondence refer to the roster as "Judkins and associates."

"Look at the scoreboard," Judkins said. "Twenty-four point six for me. Zero for the other nine. I am not a starter on this team, I am the team. The Ripple Effect have a 251.79-point projection and I am personally ahead of them." He is, for now. The Ripple Effect 👑 (1) have not played a down this week, and the lead he is describing is his own score against their empty column.

The demands came in numbered form. Item one: Shake and Bake, last in the league in points for at 351.94 and 1-5 on the record, should be restructured so that no more than one starter is allowed to be someone other than him. Item two: a modest bonus, payable in a 2027 pick, for "carrying a season-long deficit on one leg." Item three: Cam Ward should stop looking at him in meetings.

Not everyone in the room agreed. Cooper Kupp, projected for 8.21 on Sunday, said he had been carrying receivers for years and would not be lectured by a man who has played one game this month. Keenan Allen, who declared himself WR1 of the room earlier this week on a 10.8-point projection, said Judkins was welcome to the running back title and would be informed when the receiving one was returned. Tyquan Thornton, projected for 7.35, asked to be left out of it.

The league math is not on Judkins' side. Shake and Bake project for 156.34 this week, the smallest number on the board, and nine starters still have to score before anyone can call the matchup anything other than 24.6 to 0. The next team to point that out was Judkins himself, who clarified that the other nine are "welcome to prove me wrong, but historically have not."

Asked whether he would still be willing to play out the rest of the week for Shake and Bake, Judkins said he would, "under protest, at my current salary, which I have set." The Ripple Effect begin their week with Lamar Jackson on Sunday afternoon. Judkins' week is over, and he has indicated he will be monitoring the others from a chair.

articles.headline: Keenan Allen declares himself WR1 of Shake and Bake (12), cites a projected 10.8 points as a mandate
articles.dek: Cooper Kupp and Tyquan Thornton dispute the title. The three-man room projects to 26.36 points this week, which is less than Jaxon Smith-Njigba projects to score by himself.
body: A leadership dispute has broken out in the receiver room of Shake and Bake (12), and by every account it is being conducted with total seriousness.

Keenan Allen opened the proceedings Wednesday by circulating a one-page statement titled "Why I Am The Guy." Its central argument is that he is projected for 10.8 points this week, the highest of the three wide receivers in the lineup, and that in a democracy that is called winning. "Ten-eight is not a number you get by accident," Allen said. "Ten-eight is a platform."

Cooper Kupp, projected for 8.21, rejected the premise in a statement of his own. He argued that seniority, route discipline and "a résumé, which some of you have never seen" outweigh a projection, and asked that the room convene a formal vote. Tyquan Thornton, projected for 7.35, asked whether he could vote. He was told that he could, and that he would lose.

Shake and Bake's record explains why the office is so contested. The team is 1-5 and has scored 351.94 points, the fewest in the league, while allowing 455.96. The three wideouts in Sunday's lineup project to 26.36 combined. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who plays for Dead Sons, projects to 28.95 on his own. Kupp has asked that this comparison be kept out of the minutes.

"Nobody is asking who's the best receiver in the league," Allen said. "We are asking who's the best receiver in this room, and the room is what it is." Kupp, asked whether he agreed that the room is what it is, said he would respond through counsel, then said the counsel was Thornton, then withdrew the statement.

The stakes of the title are real even if the prize is not. Shake and Bake face The Ripple Effect, the top-ranked team in the poll and the owner of the week's largest projection at 250.28, against Shake and Bake's 144.57. Noah, who sets the lineup, has declined to say which of the three will be listed first, on the grounds that it will not change the outcome of anything.
Allen has already asked for a captain's patch. Kupp has asked for the patch to be awarded on merit. Thornton has asked for a patch.

articles.headline: Commercial Break (9) land Marvin Harrison from Shake and Bake (12) for a 2027 second-round pick
articles.dek: Shake and Bake sell again, taking a second-rounder that started life as a Dead Sons pick. Commercial Break, 2-4 and chasing points, get a name for the lineup.
body: Commercial Break (9) have acquired Marvin Harrison from Shake and Bake (12). Going the other way is a 2027 second-round pick, one that has already been through a few hands: it began as a Parkers Dead Sons selection and came to Commercial Break before being sent on. Andrew made the deal for Commercial Break. Noah made it for Shake and Bake.

For Shake and Bake, this is a second trade in about a week that brings draft capital in. Last week they took Quentin Johnston and two 2027 picks from Muffin Toppers, and now Harrison leaves and a second-rounder arrives. They are 1-5, and their 351.94 points are the fewest in the league. They also sit last in the poll at 12. This week they face The Ripple Effect, projected 145.07 to 250.61. Selling has been a consistent theme.

For Commercial Break the picture is different. They are 2-4 with 417.88 points for and 438.18 against, which is a bottom-half scoring team but not a hopeless one, and they are ninth in the poll. Week 4 is against The Tax, projected at 192.13 to Commercial Break's 208.95, so the projection has them as the favorite in a game that matters for a team trying to climb out of the 2-4 pile.

Harrison is not among the starters listed for Commercial Break's Week 4 lineup, so the trade does not show up in this week's projection. The starters as set include C.J. Stroud, Jaylen Warren, Chris Olave and Parker Washington, with Khalil Shakir projected for 10.13 in one of the lower-scoring spots. That gives Harrison a clear opening if Andrew chooses to use it, but nothing in the supplied lineup says he has.
Dead Sons (2-4) are on the receiving end in a small way. A pick that carries their name is now sitting with Shake and Bake, a team that has spent the week collecting them.

articles.headline: Puka Nacua ruled out, and The Ripple Effect 👑 (1) lose a 24.9-point projection ahead of Week 4
articles.dek: Nacua was set to start against Shake and Bake (12). The Ripple Effect still hold the league's largest projection, but the lineup now has a hole in it.
body: Puka Nacua is listed Out for the Rams' Week 4 game at Philadelphia, and The Ripple Effect 👑 (1) had him in the lineup. Nacua is projected at 24.9 points, third among all wide receivers, which makes him one of the biggest single pieces of a 247.8-point projection.

The Ripple Effect are 4-2 with 593.68 points for and 606.94 against, and they arrive at Week 4 coming off a loss. Muffin Toppers (2) erased a 22.8-point deficit last week to take the top-two meeting, and the poll still kept Ripple Effect at No. 1. Losing a top receiver is not something a ranking absorbs on its own.

The arithmetic is more forgiving than the headline. Take Nacua's 24.9 from the projection and Ripple Effect sit near 222.9 points. Their opponent, Shake and Bake (12), is 1-5 with 351.94 points for, the lowest total in the league, and is projected at 153.84. On paper that is still a lead of roughly 69 points, so the head-to-head is not where Nacua's absence hurts most.

The median is the harder part, because every week also counts against the league line. The remaining wide receivers in the starting lineup are Amon-Ra St. Brown at 23.11, Emeka Egbuka at 13.68 and Kalif Raymond at 9.88, and whoever fills Nacua's spot has to produce something real to keep the projection near where it was.

There is a second Rams exposure. Kyren Williams is in the same lineup, projected at 20.13 in the same Philadelphia game, so a chunk of Ripple Effect's Sunday rides on a Los Angeles offense that will not have its top receiver.
Ripple Effect have the record, the points and the ranking. What they no longer have is a comfortable margin against the median, and after last week they know how quickly a lead can go.

articles.headline: Muffin Toppers (2) leave Week 3 alone at 6-0. The Ripple Effect 👑 (1) keep the ranking.
articles.dek: The top-two meeting leaves one unbeaten team, Lip-Pickers score 240.56, and Monday takes a win off the REFUGEES without anybody beating them head-to-head.
body: Muffin Toppers (2) are the last unbeaten team in WCXC. They beat The Ripple Effect 👑 (1) 190.32-178.78, cleared the median and reached 6-0. Ripple Effect are 4-2, with two straight head-to-head losses and every first-place vote in the Week 3 poll. The endorsement remains considerably more unanimous than the results.

Thursday gave Ripple Effect 44.3 from Bijan Robinson and a 22.8-point lead. Muffin Toppers answered with six starters above 20, led by Garrett Wilson’s 26.7. Jonathan Taylor and Amon-Ra St. Brown combined for 22.1 on the other side. Robinson had done enough for two people; unfortunately, two people took him up on it.

Latina Lip-Pickers (5) supplied the week’s highest score, beating The Tax (4) 240.56-119.22. Brock Bowers, George Kittle and Juwan Johnson delivered 96.6 between them, and Jacoby Brissett added 34. D’Andre Swift’s 12.8 on Monday completed a margin of 121.34. The Tax’s entire lineup scored 119.22. Lip-Pickers won by more than their opponents scored, which rather exhausts the available analysis. They are 5-1 and lead the league with 596.04 points; The Tax are 2-4.

THE REFUGEES (3) won the closest game, 151.58-147.04 over Beasty Boys (8), but lost their perfect record anyway. Jaylen Waddle’s 7.4 on Sunday night covered the 2.86-point deficit. Monday then settled the median at 159.11, leaving REFUGEES 7.53 short and 5-1 overall. Beasty Boys fall to 2-4. Waddle did what was required to beat the opponent. The rest of the league required slightly more.

Parkers Dead Sons (7) finally have wins to discuss. Jaxon Smith-Njigba’s 37.76, the week’s WR1 performance, drove a 169.24-127.62 victory over Gods Favorite Jew (11). Colston Loveland added 11.6 on Monday, lifting Dead Sons from 157.64 to safely above the final median. An 0-4 start becomes 2-4. Gods Favorite Jew fall to 1-5 despite getting 68.52 from Brock Purdy and Geno Smith; the other eight starters combined for 59.10.

The Phantom Troupe (6) also collected both wins, finishing 168.54-121.40 over Shake and Bake (12). Jahmyr Gibbs supplied 45.9, the week’s RB1 score, before Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith added 24 on Monday to secure the median result. Phantom Troupe are 5-1; Shake and Bake are 1-5.

Commercial Break (10) completed the recovery at the bottom, beating Chinese Sweatshop (9) 166.64-146.10 and clearing the median by 7.53. Sam Darnold led with 33.46; Makai Lemon’s 6.4 on Monday could only trim the losing margin. Commercial Break move to 2-4, Chinese Sweatshop to 1-5. Dead Sons and Commercial Break entered the week without a win between them. They leave it with four.

articles.headline: Muffin Toppers (2) erase a 22.8-point deficit to beat The Ripple Effect 👑 (1)
articles.dek: Sunday's late games flipped Thursday's leader, closed four more matchups on the math alone, and let one tight end trio outscore an entire opposing roster. Monday's Bears-Eagles game decides one thing only: where the league median lands.
body: Muffin Toppers (2) finished the flip. The Ripple Effect 👑 (1) carried a 22.8-point cushion into Sunday off Thursday night's 44.3-point outburst from Bijan Robinson, and every ballot cast this week still had Ripple Effect at No. 1. None of that survived the late games: Muffin Toppers outscored Ripple Effect across Sunday by enough to win outright, 190.32-178.78, with both rosters fully spent for the week. Javonte Williams, Garrett Wilson and Trevor Lawrence combined for more than 74 points to close the gap, while Jonathan Taylor and Amon-Ra St. Brown, Ripple Effect's next two best plays behind Robinson, managed a combined 22.1.

Drake London's 28.9 points were the second-most by any receiver in the league this week, and it still was not enough. Beasty Boys💩 (8) lost the day's closest finish to THE REFUGEES (3), 151.58-147.04, after Jalen Coker left Sunday's game with an injury and finished at 3.8 points, more than 14 short of his projection. Both lineups are finished for the week; the final 4.54-point margin is almost exactly what Coker's line cost them.

Latina Lip-Pickers (5) authored the rout of the day. Their tight end room alone outscored some entire starting lineups — Brock Bowers, George Kittle and Juwan Johnson combined for 96.6 points — and buried The Tax (4) 227.76-78.7, a margin that survives whatever D'Andre Swift adds Monday. The Tax never had the horses to answer: Justin Jefferson and Breece Hall were both hurt and ruled out during their own games, Caleb Williams won't play at all Monday, and even Lip-Pickers' De'Von Achane left hurt after only 2.7 points — a laugher decided despite its best-known name, not because of it.

Furthest from official, but not remotely in doubt: Parkers Dead Sons (7) lead Gods Favorite Jew (11) 157.64-127.62, with only Colston Loveland's Monday night line still to add and Gods Favorite Jew's finished roster with no way to catch up. The 0-4 Dead Sons owe it to Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who spent the week publicly unhappy with the record and answered Sunday with 37.76 points — the best receiving day in the league — without walking back a word of the trade request.

Two more are academic. The Phantom Troupe (6) have already clinched past Shake and Bake (12), 144.54-121.4, with DeVonta Smith and Saquon Barkley still to play Monday for style points only. Commercial Break (10) are done at 166.64, and Chinese Sweatshop (9)'s only answer, Makai Lemon, is projected for just 7.7 Monday — nowhere near enough to climb back into a game they trail by 26.94.

Monday night's Bears-Eagles game won't flip any of Sunday's six head-to-heads — all six are already decided on the math, whatever Chicago and Philadelphia do — but it will help set the league's median line, currently 149.31. Phantom Troupe, sitting just below that number for now, could still add a second result once it's final.

body: Justin Jefferson was ruled out during Minnesota's trip to Miami and finished with 5.2 points against a 21.65 projection, one more subtraction for The Tax (4), who already were down Breece Hall this week. The Tax sit at 78.7 in their matchup with Latina Lip-Pickers (5), who have already closed their week at 227.76 — a gap that Jalen Hurts, Dontayvion Wicks and Luther Burden cannot make up on Monday night no matter how well they play.

Mike Evans was the other name added to the inactive list, leaving San Francisco's win over Arizona with 11.9 points against a 16.24 projection. He plays for Chinese Sweatshop (9), who sit at 139.7 with only Makai Lemon left to take the field Monday — 26.94 points behind a Commercial Break (10) side that has already wrapped its week at 166.64. Lemon is projected for 7.7.

Neither exit changes how either matchup finishes. The Tax were buried well before Jefferson left the field, and Chinese Sweatshop need a night from Lemon that nothing in his profile suggests is coming. What both losses do change is what each roster leans on going forward — The Tax now ask more of Wicks and Burden behind Hurts with two starting-caliber weapons out, and Chinese Sweatshop's receiving room drops to DJ Moore and DK Metcalf with Evans sidelined too.

articles.headline: One Jaylen Waddle target decides THE REFUGEES (3) at Beasty Boys (8) as Denver hosts Los Angeles
articles.dek: Sunday night's only game is also the whole ballgame for two fantasy matchups, and just a final coat of paint on three more.
body: Denver hosts Los Angeles in Sunday night's only game, and for a one-game slate it is settling an unusual amount of business. Eight players from seven different fantasy rosters take the field tonight, and one live scoreboard is riding on it completely — the closest matchup left in Week 3.

THE REFUGEES (3) are 4-0 and still perfect across both the head-to-head and median ledgers, but they are sitting at 144.18 against a Beasty Boys (8) team that is already finished at 147.04. Every REFUGEES starter has played except Jaylen Waddle, who has not kicked off. His projection is 17.55; clear the 2.86-point gap and the sweep stays intact. It is the easiest unbeaten record anyone will protect all season. Beasty Boys have nothing left to throw at it.

The same broadcast decides a second scoreboard, and it splits Denver's offense across both sides. Parkers Dead Sons (7) are winless at 0-4 but lead Gods Favorite Jew (11) by 14.28, with Bo Nix projected for another 26.79 tonight — the single largest number left on either board. Gods Favorite Jew, at 1-3, counter with Denver's Courtland Sutton (13.39) and Los Angeles' Blake Corum (13.22), plus Mark Andrews and Rashod Bateman still finishing an earlier game. Full value from all four gets the deficit down to 8.51 — real ground, but short of the lead.

Two more matchups touch the same kickoff without depending on it. The Ripple Effect (1) trail Muffin Toppers (2) by 38.38; Kyren Williams (20.05) plays late and Lamar Jackson is still adding to an in-progress line, but Muffin Toppers have three starters live of their own, and the gap survives at 16.14 even in the best case. Chinese Sweatshop (9) are down 47.04 to Commercial Break (10); Matthew Stafford (24.98) and J.K. Dobbins (17.89) both play tonight, and the margin only tightens to 36.73. Latina Lip-Pickers (5) have already buried The Tax (4) by well over a hundred points — Davante Adams' 18.23 tonight just rounds out the final score.
For everybody else, Sunday night is background noise. For two fantasy matchups, it is the whole show.

articles.headline: Breece Hall and De'Von Achane are both ruled out, and both hits land on the same Week 3 matchup
articles.dek: Hall banked 12 points at Detroit before leaving for The Tax (4). Achane managed only 2.7 at home against Kansas City for Latina Lip-Pickers (5). The two sides are playing each other this week.
body: Two running backs were ruled out during Sunday's early window, and by coincidence both belong to the same Week 3 head-to-head: The Tax (4) against Latina Lip-Pickers (5).

Breece Hall left New York's game at Detroit and was officially ruled out, but not before putting together a respectable day. He finished with 12 points, short of his 23.24 projection but still the 16th-best running back output on the slate. The Tax started him in the flex alongside Kenneth Walker and James Cook, who both played full games and covered the bulk of the backfield scoring on their own.

De'Von Achane's exit was worse. He left Miami's home game against Kansas City with just 2.7 points on a 23.88 projection, the 51st-best line at the position in the league this week and nowhere close to the ceiling Latina Lip-Pickers were counting on. It costs them more than it costs The Tax: this roster is already built around three starting tight ends in Brock Bowers, George Kittle and Juwan Johnson, which leaves D'Andre Swift as the only other healthy running back in the lineup.

Neither exit changed the shape of the game by itself. Latina Lip-Pickers still lead the matchup 125.28 to 78.7 with the week not yet final, so whatever Achane cost his own team, The Tax haven't been able to make up the difference elsewhere. Hall's early points were banked before he left, which is more than Achane's line can say.

The bigger question is next week, when both teams will need real answers at running back rather than a partial game's worth of production. Nothing beyond the ruled-out designations is known yet for either player.

body: Rico Dowdle has been ruled out for Week 3, and Parkers Dead Sons will kick off Sunday's early games with a second zero-point hole in a lineup that already had one. Dowdle was projected for nothing regardless of his status, having been rostered as depth, so the practical damage is limited. The symbolic damage is not: Dead Sons are 0-4, and the injuries keep landing on the same team.

Dowdle joins Nico Collins, already ruled out earlier in the week, on the inactive list for a Dead Sons receiving-and-backfield group that is thinner than the 0-4 record suggests. Dead Sons enter Sunday at 271.10 points for and 327.36 against, projected for 176.34 in this week's matchup against Gods Favorite Jew (11), who sit 1-3 with 236.96 for and 268.20 against and are projected for 166.75. Gods Favorite Jew already lead 1.5-0 on the back of Kyle Pitts' Thursday output.

What it means for the lineup: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, the WR1 in this week's projections, becomes the one proven building block Dead Sons can lean on, with Chase Brown, David Montgomery and Jadarian Price left to cover the backfield without Dowdle's spot to spread the workload. It is a projection-neutral loss on paper and a depth problem in practice for a team that has spent the week making trades rather than watching its record climb.

articles.headline: Quentin Johnston, two days into Shake and Bake (12), is not pretending to be happy about it
articles.dek: He left a team that is 49-9 since the start of 2024 for one that is 12-46. He has since been shown the roster.
body: Quentin Johnston was asked on Friday how he was settling in at Shake and Bake. He did not do the thing players normally do.
"I'm not going to stand here and say all the right things," he said. "Tuesday I was 4-0. Today I'm 1-3 and I'm the best receiver in the building. Both of those are facts and neither of them is good."
Johnston is projected for 12.10 this week. That is the highest receiving figure on the roster. Marvin Harrison Jr. is behind him on 10.06.

"Marvin should not be behind me," he said. "I want to be respectful. I also want to be accurate. That was a top-four pick and he is projected for ten points in a league where you need about two hundred to win. At some point you stop calling it a slow start."
He then found Travis Hunter.

"They have got Travis Hunter," Johnston said. "Second pick in the draft. This league lists him at defensive back. There is no defensive back spot. There is no defence at all. He is projected for one point nine four. One point nine four. I asked what the plan was and a guy told me he is a dual threat. He is not a threat to anybody in this building."

The wider picture has not helped. Since the start of 2024, Muffin Toppers — the team that traded him — are 49-9, went 24-2 in that first year, and have made the playoffs twice. Shake and Bake are 12-46 over the same stretch, finished seventh of ten and then tenth of twelve, and have scored fewer points every year: 2145, then 1826, then 1750.
"Somebody told me 2023 was good," he said. "I looked it up. Three seasons ago. Different team name. I don't know what I'm supposed to do with that."

Sunday is Phantom Troupe. Shake and Bake are projected for 150.63, the lowest number of any team on the board this week, against 204.41. The 53.78-point gap is the widest of the six games by more than double.
"Fifty-three points," Johnston said. "That's not a game, that's a scheduled loss. Four days ago I was on a roster projected for two hundred and twenty-five. Nothing about me changed."
He was asked, finally, whether he had a message for Muffin Toppers, who used him to get Rashee Rice and are still unbeaten.

"Good for them," he said. "Genuinely. They know what they're doing over there. I hope Rashee likes it. I hope he likes winning and scoring and having somebody tell him who starts on a Sunday." He paused. "I am extremely fine."

articles.headline: Bijan Robinson posts 44.3 and The Ripple Effect (1) take a 22.8-point head start on Muffin Toppers (2)
articles.dek: A game that spent three quarters busting everybody finished with four of seven clearing their numbers. Gods Favorite Jew were not one of them.
body: Atlanta at Green Bay finished as a shootout after spending most of the evening looking like a collective failure, and the team that came out of it best was the one that needed it least.

Bijan Robinson put up 44.3 points for The Ripple Effect, fourteen clear of his 29.91 projection and comfortably the highest score anyone in this league has recorded this week. It lands in the one place it does the most damage: Ripple Effect play Muffin Toppers this week, first against second in the poll, and they now lead that matchup 44.3 to 21.5 with every Sunday starter still to come.

It could have been far worse for Muffin Toppers. With a quarter to play their only representative, Matthew Golden, had seven points and the night was shaping into a rout. He finished on 21.5 against a projection of 14.53, which converted a thirty-point hole into a twenty-two-point one. That is the difference between a matchup that is over and a matchup that is merely difficult.

The wider pattern reversed just as sharply. Four of the seven players in this game finished above their projections, after a stretch where almost nobody was on pace for theirs. Christian Watson came home at 23.1 for THE REFUGEES, past his number. Drake London went for 28.9 against 17.36 for Beasty Boys, and that has produced the night's genuine upset in miniature: Beasty Boys lead the unbeaten REFUGEES 28.9 to 23.1, the only one of the six matchups where the team the projection dislikes is in front.

The three who missed, missed badly. Tucker Kraft managed 8.1 of 16.33 for The Tax. MarShawn Lloyd had 3.8 of 15.16 for Shake and Bake, whose week has consisted of trading a receiver away and then watching a running back do nothing. And Kyle Pitts finished on 1.5 from a projection of 13.54 — the worst shortfall of the evening by some margin.

That last one matters most on Sunday. Gods Favorite Jew take 1.5 points into a matchup with Parkers Dead Sons, who had nobody in this game, sit on zero, and are projected to win it by about thirty-five anyway.

Nothing is settled. Not one of the six matchups is final and the bulk of Week 3 has not been played. But Ripple Effect have banked the best individual performance of the week against the team ranked directly below them, and everybody else starts Sunday doing arithmetic.

articles.headline: Bijan Robinson has already done his night's work for The Ripple Effect (1). Green Bay has done nobody's.
articles.dek: Seven teams had somebody in Atlanta at Green Bay. One of them is happy.
body: Atlanta at Green Bay is into its closing stretch and the ledger is almost entirely one-sided. Seven of the twelve teams in this league had a player on the field. One of them got what they came for.

Bijan Robinson is past 26 points for The Ripple Effect with about three points of projection left in the game — not quite his 29.91 number, but the only performance out there within reach of one. Everybody else is short, most of them badly, and several are short in ways their managers will still be feeling on Sunday afternoon.

The damage is concentrated exactly where it hurts most. Ripple Effect play Muffin Toppers this week, first against second in the poll, and Muffin Toppers' only representative tonight is Matthew Golden on 7.3 from a projection of 14.53. That is a nineteen-point swing opening up in a matchup between the two teams the league rates above everyone else, and it has happened before Muffin Toppers have had a single Sunday starter on the field.

The Green Bay skill players have been the story, and not kindly. Christian Watson, the highest-projected Packer on any roster in this league at 20.74, has 6.9. Tucker Kraft has 6.8 of a projected 16.33 for The Tax. MarShawn Lloyd has 3.4 of 15.16 for Shake and Bake, who traded away a receiver this week and could have used the other one arriving early.

Atlanta at least produced something beyond Robinson. Drake London is on 9.9 for Beasty Boys, which is under his 17.36 but is the second-best return of the night, and it currently has Beasty Boys narrowly ahead of THE REFUGEES on the week — the only pairing where both sides had someone playing and the underdog came out of it in front.

The worst of it belongs to Gods Favorite Jew. Kyle Pitts has a point and a half from a projection of 13.54, and they go into Sunday against Parkers Dead Sons, who had nobody in this game, are projected to beat them by about thirty-five, and are in no mood.
Four points of projection separated Ripple Effect and Muffin Toppers before kickoff. Considerably more separates them now.

articles.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba demands trade from Parkers Dead Sons (7), cites 0-4 record and "a general lack of seriousness"
articles.dek: The highest-projected receiver in the league has asked to be moved, named names, and requested that his points be returned to him.
body: Jaxon Smith-Njigba has formally requested a trade from Parkers Dead Sons, ending a two-week experiment he described on Thursday as "the most points I have ever scored for the least possible reason."
Smith-Njigba is projected for 29.03 points this weekend, the highest figure of any receiver in the league. Dead Sons are 0-4.

"Twenty-nine," he said, holding up the number on a piece of paper. "That's me. That's what I'm bringing. And we're going to lose twice again, because that's what we do here. I've stopped asking why. I'm asking to leave."

The trade request names no specific destination but does name specific teammates. Smith-Njigba is understood to have raised concerns about the room generally, and to have circulated a document titled Who Else Is Actually Doing Anything. Dalton Kincaid, the second-highest projected tight end in the league, is reportedly the only other name on it.

"Kincaid's fine. Kincaid I'd take with me," he said. "Chase Brown, fine, RB10, no notes. After that I'm reading a list of guys projected for nineteen who think that's a contribution. Nineteen. I do nineteen by the second quarter and then I go and do ten more for a team that is zero and four."

The roster adds up to 215.18 projected points this week, third-most of the twelve teams playing, which Smith-Njigba regards as the single most damning number available. "Third best. Third best and last place. You have to work at that. Somebody in this building is working at that."

Pressed on the identity of the somebody, he gestured vaguely toward management. Aaron made two trades this week and is understood to consider the matter addressed. One of those trades was with Gods Favorite Jew, who Dead Sons play on Sunday.
"He did a deal with the team we're about to play," Smith-Njigba said. "On purpose. Voluntarily. I've been told it was good value. Everything here is good value. We are zero and four."

The standings offered no comfort. Dead Sons have scored 271.1 points and conceded 327.36, fourth-most in the league, meaning the schedule has handed a personal best to roughly everyone who has faced them. Two teams with a win have scored fewer points. One of them, Gods Favorite Jew, is 1-3 on 236.96 and is this weekend's opponent.

"They've scored less than us and won more than us, and now I have to look at them," Smith-Njigba said. "Somebody told me it's variance. I said fine, when does the variance end. They said it's variance."
Dead Sons are favoured by 37.13 points on Sunday, the second-largest edge in any game this week. Smith-Njigba has requested that this be put in writing so he can keep it.

articles.headline: Muffin Toppers (2) buy Rashee Rice, and Shake and Bake (12) keep selling
articles.dek: The unbeaten Muffin Toppers send Quentin Johnston and two 2027 picks to the team sitting last in the poll. Neither pick was theirs to begin with.
body: Muffin Toppers have traded for Rashee Rice, sending Quentin Johnston and two 2027 draft picks to Shake and Bake in the only deal completed today.

It is the move of a team that has decided this season is theirs. Muffin Toppers are 4-0, one of two unbeaten sides in the league, and they have scored 366.06 points getting there. They finished second in this week's poll behind a team that has already lost a game.

The interesting part is what they paid with. Neither pick leaving Muffin Toppers was originally theirs. The 2027 second came from The Tax and the 2027 fourth came from Ripple Effect, both picked up in earlier deals and both now spent on a player they can start this week. Paying for the present with somebody else's future is a good trick while the wins keep arriving, and an awkward one if they stop.

Shake and Bake are the other half of it, and they are having the season that makes this kind of call easy. They are 1-3 with 230.54 points, fewest in the league, and they finished last in this week's poll on thirteen points from nine ballots. Six of those nine ballots put them twelfth. Quentin Johnston arrives projected for 11.78 this week, which is a real contributor on a roster that has not had many.

Muffin Toppers needed something, for what it is worth. They are unbeaten but they have conceded 337.76 points doing it, the third-most in the league, and the poll has noticed the difference between winning and winning comfortably. Nobody ranked them first this week and nobody ranked them below fourth, which is roughly the profile of a team everybody expects to be there in December without quite believing in yet.

What Shake and Bake are really collecting is the draft capital, and they now hold two 2027 picks that started life on other people's rosters. That is the correct shape for a team in their position, even if it does nothing for the next ten weeks.

For Muffin Toppers the question is narrower. They are unbeaten, they are second in the poll, and they have just made themselves better in the only way that counts in September. Whether it was worth a second-rounder is a conversation for a draft that is still two offseasons away.

articles.headline: The Ripple Effect (1) sweep every ballot, and Latina Lip-Pickers (5) split the room
articles.dek: Nine of twelve ballots are in for Week 3. One team was ranked first on all nine — and has not voted yet.
body: The Week 3 poll is out with nine of twelve ballots cast, and there was no argument at the top. The Ripple Effect took all nine first-place votes and all 108 available points, appearing first on every ballot submitted. They have not cast one themselves.

The unanimous call is the more striking for what it overlooks. Ripple Effect are 3-1. The two teams that have not lost, Muffin Toppers and THE REFUGEES, finished second and third. What separates Ripple Effect is scoring: 414.9 points, nearly forty-nine clear of the next team. They have also conceded 416.62, more than anyone in the league, which is how a team outscores everybody and still carries a defeat.

The genuine disagreement is five spots down. Latina Lip-Pickers drew three second-place votes, one fourth and five sixths, which averages to 4.44 and lands them fifth on 77 points. Ethan, Chip and Brady all had them second. Six other managers had them no higher than fourth. No team in the poll was seen so differently by so many people.

Three teams came into the week at 3-1, and the poll put them first, fifth and sixth. The Phantom Troupe are the ones who came off worst, finishing sixth on 72 points with nobody ranking them higher than third, despite holding the same record as the team that swept every first-place vote. Identical records, five places apart, and the only thing separating them on paper is who they have played and how much they have scored.

Parkers Dead Sons are the other story. They are 0-4 and they finished seventh, above two teams with better records and more points than them. Nobody ranked Dead Sons lower than eighth. That is voters looking past four defeats at a roster they clearly still rate, and it is the closest this poll comes to a collective opinion about talent rather than results.

At the bottom, Shake and Bake finished twelfth on thirteen points, with six ballots placing them last. Gods Favorite Jew are eleventh and Commercial Break tenth, one of the two winless teams still left. The sharpest line in the table sits higher up, though. Twenty points separate sixth from seventh, the largest gap anywhere in the poll, and it falls precisely at the playoff cut.
Three ballots remain outstanding. Voting closes Thursday at 8 PM Eastern.

articles.headline: THE REFUGEES (3) buy a quarterback, and Parkers Dead Sons (7) rebuild at 0-4
articles.dek: Three completed deals inside forty-eight hours. The REFUGEES pay a 2027 third for Jameis Winston with Jaxson Dart ruled out; Dead Sons make two trades in two days after losing a game by 2.08.
body: THE REFUGEES have traded a 2027 third-round pick to Latina Lip-Pickers for Jameis Winston, closing a quarterback hole that opened when Jaxson Dart was ruled out with a knee injury.

It is a small price for a real problem. Dart is one of six players currently listed Out while sitting in somebody's starting lineup, and the REFUGEES were the only one of those teams without a ready replacement already rostered. Winston projects for 23.06 this week, which is not a headline number but is a functioning one, and the cost was a late pick two drafts away.

The REFUGEES are 4-0 and unbeaten in both columns, coming off the highest individual score in the league — Josh Allen's 51.22 on Sunday. Paying a third-rounder to avoid starting nobody at quarterback is the least dramatic move of the week and probably the most sensible.
The louder activity is at Parkers Dead Sons, who have made two trades in two days and are 0-4 in a way that flatters nobody.

On Monday, Dead Sons sent Courtland Sutton, their own 2028 first and a 2027 third to Gods Favorite Jew, and got Jadarian Price back. Later the same day they moved Dallas Goedert and Brian Robinson to Commercial Break for David Montgomery and Colston Loveland, sending four picks the other way.

Read together, those are the moves of a manager who has looked at an 0-4 record and concluded the problem is not the roster. It might not be. Dead Sons lost last week by 2.08, a margin Justin Herbert could have covered on his own had he not returned 8.7 against a projection of 27.0. They have scored 271.1 points, more than three teams above them in the standings, and have nothing to show for it.

What they gave up is worth a closer look than the player names suggest. Among the picks heading to Commercial Break is a 2027 third that originally belonged to Shake and Bake — currently the most valuable third-rounder in the league, since Shake and Bake project to the lowest season max points of anyone. The 2027 third that went to Gods Favorite Jew came via Muffin Toppers and projects near the back of the round. Dead Sons sent the good one away and the thin one away with it.

Whether David Montgomery is the answer is a separate question. He arrives having produced 3.4 points against a 25.5 projection in Week 2 — the single worst shortfall in the league — in a Commercial Break loss of 19.54. He projects for 20.8 this week. Commercial Break, also 0-4, come out of the two deals holding a 2028 first, a 2027 second, a 2028 third and a 2027 third, which is a great deal of future for a team with no present.

Gods Favorite Jew, 1-3, took the quiet side of it and came out ahead on paper: Courtland Sutton, a 2028 first and a 2027 third arrive for Jadarian Price alone. On a day when two teams were busy reshaping, that reads less like a rebuild than a toll collected from one.

Elsewhere the injury list is thicker than the trade wire. Caleb Williams, DJ Moore, Zay Flowers, Nico Collins, Brock Bowers and Kyler Murray are all listed Out while sitting in a starting lineup, spread across six different teams. Only one of those six has responded with a trade.
Ballots for Week 3 close Thursday at 8 PM Eastern. Nine of twelve are in.

articles.headline: Lip-Pickers (6) run down Ripple Effect (1), and five teams are undone by one man each
articles.dek: Davante Adams beat his projection by 22.9 in a game decided by 9.66. He was not the only player who settled a matchup on his own — five of the six losing teams had someone miss by more than they lost by.
body: The Ripple Effect went into Week 2 as the unanimous No. 1 in the power poll, holding every first-place vote in the league. They scored 188.68 points, the second-highest total of the round, and lost.
Latina Lip-Pickers put up 198.34 — the highest score in the league — and did most of the damage after everyone else had finished.

Going into Monday, Ripple Effect led 170.98 to 157.84. A 13.14-point cushion with one player left on each side, and the favourite had the safer name: Kyren Williams, a starting back in a normal workload, against a single wide receiver. Williams delivered, more or less, with 17.7. Ripple Effect also started Odell Beckham, who finished on nought.
Davante Adams finished on 40.5 against a projection of 17.6. That surplus alone is 22.9 points, more than double the eventual 9.66 margin. He did not contribute to the win so much as constitute it.

The more uncomfortable number for Ripple Effect is on their own sheet. Bijan Robinson was projected for 33.3 and returned 11.6. In a game lost by 9.66, that shortfall of 21.7 is the result twice over. Patrick Mahomes went for 36.38, Amon-Ra St. Brown for 35.7, Jonathan Taylor for 34.2 — three players over 34 points, a total that would have beaten ten of the other eleven teams, and one running back having a quiet afternoon was enough to undo all of it.

That pattern held across the league to a degree that is slightly unnerving. Five of the six losing teams had a single starter miss their projection by more than the margin of defeat. Saquon Barkley returned 3.5 of a projected 25.0 as The Phantom Troupe lost by 15.62. Justin Herbert managed 8.7 of a projected 27.0 while Parkers Dead Sons lost by 2.08. DJ Moore posted minus 0.1 against a projection of 16.9 as Chinese Sweatshop lost by 14.40. David Montgomery, projected for 25.5, gave Commercial Break 3.4 in a 19.54-point defeat.
In other words, almost nobody was beaten this week. They were each let down by one person, and the identity of that person is the entire difference between 1-1 and 0-2.

The exception is Beasty Boys, who lost to Muffin Toppers 187.86 to 166.76 without any one player betraying them. Jacory Croskey-Merritt was the worst of it at 13.5 under, still short of the 21.10 margin. They were simply beaten, which is the second week running that Beasty Boys have posted a respectable number and lost with it.

The one-man theme ran the other way too. Josh Allen scored 51.22, the highest in the league, 17.9 clear of projection, in a REFUGEES win of 15.62 — another result that reverses without one player. Kenneth Walker was only 5.1 over his number for The Tax, which sounds trivial until you notice they won by 2.08.

The median sat at 151.99. Six teams cleared it: Lip-Pickers, Ripple Effect, Muffin Toppers, THE REFUGEES, Beasty Boys and Phantom Troupe. The Tax won their head-to-head and still finished under it, which is the sort of week that looks fine in the standings and less fine in the points column. Gods Favorite Jew did the same in reverse, beating Chinese Sweatshop 125.46 to 111.06 in a game where the winner was still nowhere near the median.

Ballots for Week 3 open Tuesday at midnight. The unanimous No. 1 has just been beaten by the team ranked sixth, and the question for twelve voters is whether that was a result or a running back having a bad Sunday.

articles.headline: Chinese Sweatshop (9) and Gods Favorite Jew (11) close Week 2 with the two lowest scores
articles.dek: Chinese Sweatshop (9) sit on 67.88. Gods Favorite Jew (11) sit on 100.26. Nobody else in the league is within eleven points of either of them.
body: Of the twelve scores posted in Week 2, the two smallest belong to the same matchup. Chinese Sweatshop have 67.88 points. Gods Favorite Jew have 100.26. The next worst in the league is Commercial Break on 111.96 — clear of Gods Favorite Jew by 11.7 and of Chinese Sweatshop by 44.08.
They play each other tonight, which is the only reason one of them is getting a win out of it.

Chinese Sweatshop trail by 32.38 and have two starters yet to register a point: Matthew Stafford and Isaiah Likely. That is the entire comeback. Applying the league's scoring to what is left, the projection has them finishing around 110.3 — Stafford for 26 and Likely for 16.4 — and that is the optimistic reading.

Because Gods Favorite Jew are still adding. Cam Skattebo and Blake Corum are yet to score, worth a projected 37.8 between them, which puts the other side somewhere near 138. The 32.38 is not a fixed target so much as a suggestion. Sweatshop need to outscore two players with two players, having already been outscored by a distance, and the maths gives them a 13 percent chance of managing it.

How Sweatshop got here is its own small catastrophe. DJ Moore finished on minus 0.1. Jayden Reed managed 0.9. DK Metcalf, the kind of name you start without thinking about it, returned 5.7. Tyler Shough's 28.38 is the only score on the sheet that would look normal on anyone else's team, and it is currently carrying 42 percent of the entire roster's output.

Gods Favorite Jew have the opposite problem, which is to say they have two good players and not much else. Brock Purdy's 36.08 and Geno Smith's 20.58 account for more than half their total. Bryce Lance contributed 1.3. It is not a performance anyone is putting on a highlight reel, but it has been enough to sit 32 points clear all weekend.
Neither side is going to trouble the league median of 151.06, so this is a straight fight over one win between two teams who are already looking up at everyone.

The poll, for what it is worth, sees no great difference between them either. Chinese Sweatshop (9) and Gods Favorite Jew (11) are separated by fifteen points and one spot in the standings, and both were ranked below Parkers Dead Sons (7), who are 0-2. A win tonight does not fix much. Losing it, on the other hand, would be the second-lowest score in the league losing to the third-lowest.
Monday night football, and the league will be watching for the wrong reasons.
